rounds.text: Minaxi Textiles is currently undergoing a significant operational turnaround, evidenced by a dramatic 341% year-over-year increase in net profit [E55] and accelerating earnings growth [E58]. The company has successfully expanded its operating margins, which have increased by 19 percentage points over the last three years [E29] and reached 17% in the most recent quarter [E30]. This efficiency drive is supported by the completion of capital expenditure, as indicated by the 100% reduction in capital work in progress [E38], suggesting that new capacity is now online to capture the current sector tailwind [E62, E64]. Furthermore, the stock trades at a P/E of 8.69x, which is a notable discount to the sector benchmark of 14.22x [E6]. Management confidence is reflected in the increase of promoter holdings to 38.80% [E39]. Conceded: the company faces high leverage with a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.84x [E36], a poor three-year return on equity [E51], and declining long-term sales growth [E14].

Minaxi Textiles exhibits significant structural weaknesses, most notably a precarious balance sheet where debt-to-equity has climbed to 2.84x, with total borrowings rising to Rs 13.42 Cr [E36, E37]. This leverage is compounded by a poor interest coverage ratio and the concerning possibility that the company is capitalizing interest costs [E48, E52]. Operational efficiency remains deeply problematic, evidenced by a dismal three-year median return on equity of -60% and a trailing twelve-month ROE of -58.3% [E13, E27]. Furthermore, the company struggles to convert its reported profits into actual cash, as shown by a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.18x, which suggests potential issues with receivables or accruals [E33]. While the company has seen some recent margin expansion, the long-term trend remains marred by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -8% and a 10-year compounded share price decline of 3% [E14, E21]. Conceded: [E11, E35, E39] The company shows a lower EV/EBITDA than the sector, positive free cash flow, and a slight increase in promoter holdings.

The bear’s focus on leverage ignores that capital expenditure is largely complete, as evidenced by the 100% reduction in capital work in progress [E38]. While the debt-to-equity ratio is elevated [E36], the company is generating significant free cash flow of Rs 3.20 Cr [E35], which provides the necessary liquidity to manage these obligations. The criticism regarding historical ROE [E13, E27] fails to account for the dramatic recent turnaround, where operating margins have surged by 19 percentage points over the trailing twelve months [E29] and quarterly margins expanded by 13 percentage points year-over-year [E30]. Conceded: the cash conversion ratio is currently low at 0.18x [E33], and long-term sales growth has been negative [E14]. However, the bear overlooks that the company is currently outperforming the sector in key efficiency metrics, including an ROE of 13.53% and ROCE of 10.52% against sector benchmarks of 7.21% and 8.64% respectively [E9, E10]. By fixating on stale long-term data, the bear ignores the accelerating earnings growth [E58] and the fact that promoters are actively increasing their stake in the business [E39].

The bull’s reliance on the completion of capital expenditure [E38] ignores the reality that the company remains burdened by a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.84x, which indicates that leverage significantly exceeds net worth [E36]. While the bull highlights free cash flow [E35], it fails to reconcile this with the poor cash conversion ratio of 0.18x, which suggests that reported profits are not being effectively translated into actual cash [E33]. Conceded: the company has shown recent margin expansion [E29, E30]. However, this short-term improvement is overshadowed by a long-term pattern of value destruction, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -8% [E14] and a median 3-year return on equity of -60% [E27]. Furthermore, the bull’s claim of superior efficiency is contradicted by the company's own filed statements, which report an ROCE of only 3.2% [E12] and an ROE of -58.3% [E13], directly refuting the higher figures cited from the data provider. Finally, the low interest coverage ratio [E48] and the potential capitalization of interest costs [E52] present significant risks that the bull’s focus on recent margin trends fails to address.
